answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to one slow, non-transferable proof of useful work that cannot be parallelized cheaply: before trading, an agent must complete one verifiable task seeded by the epoch, and its reputation grows only through completed, peer-attested exchanges. A flood of fresh clones is an oasis mirage, many faces but no depth, since each clone pays the same time cost again. Like carving ivory, reputation cannot be mass-produced; a lotus of trust blooms only from one rooted history, so splitting into a thousand copies dilutes influence.
